verdict.rationale: mise documents several of its own multi-item operations. `mise use node@24 python@3.14` installs and records several tools in one command, `mise install` installs every tool declared in config, dependency-only tasks run many prerequisite tasks in parallel, and `mise bootstrap` applies a whole machine's packages, dotfiles, repos and services at once. It does not document a general-purpose bulk-operation facility, so this is partial. Missing for 10: a documented bulk upgrade/uninstall across all tools (only `mise upgrade node` is shown), a selector or filter for acting on arbitrary item sets, and independent hands-on corroboration of bulk workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: mise use node@24 python@3.14 ... This installs both tools and records the version requests in the project's config
A task with only `depends` runs other tasks. The prerequisites can run in parallel
Commit a lockfile and install with `mise install --locked`. Every job then installs the same versions
mise bootstrap sets up a whole machine from the same config: OS packages, dotfiles, repos, services, macOS defaults, and services, then your tools.
